quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes to green.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction if you are in the correct lane and the road ahead is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: Backing up your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if you have a helper.
Only dangerous in large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always dangerous.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Always use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly for them.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly for them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot or be missed in a quick glance. Always look around carefully and watch for motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds.

questions.question: Your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed to get better traction.
Press the brakes hard to stop sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires lose contact with the road due to water, it is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check several times if needed. Watch both the traffic in front of you and the traffic beside you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. Turning right here is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction more slowly than normal.
Drive the same way you normally do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: Make all speed and direction changes slowly on snow or ice. Never use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control.

questions.question: A car cuts in front of you suddenly. What is the first thing you should do?

options.text: Honk and press the brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between you and the other car without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: A traffic light is broken and not working. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and let other vehicles go first before entering.
If the intersection looks clear, you can go without stopping.
Drive fast through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and let other vehicles go first before entering.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and let other vehicles go first before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: Which of these is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Use high beam lights in fog.
Stare at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Check your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Staring only at the road ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers will not speed up this process.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
Other drivers might make mistakes, and they prepare to react.
They expect no favors and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers might make mistakes, and they prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers expect other drivers to make mistakes and are ready to react safely to those mistakes.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped ahead to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
Change lanes and pass the bus slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn. Even then, check for children crossing before you go.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all oncoming vehicles. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. First yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: If you experience a tire blowout:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, remove your foot from the accelerator and slow down gradually. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed considerably.

questions.question: When stopped at a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if you:

options.text: Come to a complete stop first.
Wait until the light changes.
Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear. Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, most tires can move water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires lose this ability and may ride over the water like water skis.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is not unsafe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly frustrates other drivers and may cause them to make dangerous passing moves. Drive with the flow of traffic within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots, even with both rearview and outside mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than most passenger cars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is changing direction or getting narrower. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is no room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is no room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time in either direction. Do not stop on the tracks. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before stopping.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle on a hill, you should:

options.text: Have one rear wheel touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in "park" on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the road center so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it (going downhill) or gently against it (going uphill).

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause serious problems. As speed increases, crashes become more severe and injuries become worse. Increase your following distance at higher speeds so you can stop safely if needed.
